description: gridemissions is a Python toolkit for calculating and accessing emissions attributed to electricity consumption. It processes U.S. power production, demand and exchange data with generation emission factors, and includes an API client and data-handling functions. Inputs are regional grid time series and emission assumptions; outputs are electricity and embodied-emissions series used by the Stanford gridemissions display and published separately. The default sources focus on U.S. balancing areas with hourly updates, while a study period follows available EIA files. Source code is free under MIT terms. A limitation is that embodied-emissions estimates depend on data reconciliation and emission factors; they are not direct measurements at each consuming site. The software can prepare emissions inputs for grid-operation and electrification simulations. It complements electricity network models such as PyPSA (model-pypsa), but no dataset or live API was requested during review.
